# Fixture provenance

Generated by `tools/gen_fixtures.py`. Do not edit by hand.

The Python editor in `Decomp/DW4/DW4_Save_Editor` is the only known-good
implementation. These fixtures freeze its behaviour so the Rust core can be
tested without Python and without the read-only `Decomp/` tree.

| Item | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `mcd001/save.raw` | `memcards/Mcd001.ps2` -> `BASLUS-20836savedata/BASLUS-20836savedata`, extracted with the Python editor's `dw4save.load_any` |
| `mcd001/expected.json` | values read by the same module |
| `catalogue/*.json` | `dw4save.load_catalogue`, `describe_item_id` and `invalid_reason` |
| `flags/mirrors.json` | `dw4build.NORMAL_FLAG_MIRRORS`, plus the GUI's `FLAG_MIRRORS`/`FOLDER_MIRRORS` extracted by `ast` |
| `flags/presets.json` | `dw4build.STORY_PRESETS` and the GUI's, likewise |
| `builder/*.raw` | `dw4build.build_save` |
| `document/applied.raw`, `document/view.json` | `dw4save.SaveData`, driven in `App.apply` order |
| `document/validate.json` | `dw4save.CAPS` and `dw4save.upcnt_safe_cap` |

## What is executed and what is transcribed

`dw4save.py` imports cleanly and is used directly. `save_editor_gui.py`
imports `tkinter` at module scope, which is not installed here, so it can
never be imported. Two consequences:

- Its plain-literal tables (`FLAG_MIRRORS`, `STORY_PRESETS`, the labels) are
  extracted by parsing the source with `ast` and executing only the
  assignments, never the code.
- `App.collect()` and `App.apply()` cannot be run at all. `apply`'s byte
  semantics are therefore produced by driving the real
  `dw4save.SaveData` setters in the order `App.apply` uses
  (`save_editor_gui.py:1197`), and its story-mirror step is transcribed
  from `save_editor_gui.py:1234`. The ordering is verified by
  `tests/document_parity.rs`, which requires byte-identical output; the
  scripted edit set is chosen so that the deliberate divergences in
  `docs/save-format.md` section 5 do not apply.
